matches.note: R10 says the key is per (login, IP) with no per-account cap, so rotating source addresses gives a fresh budget against one account.
R7 flags the 10-digit (~33-bit) key and says the reset key shares that space, but it misses the non-cryptographic RNG and treats the reset key as mitigated.
R7 says /account/activate has no @RateLimited, which allows unbounded online guessing of the activation key.
R9 attacks the per-OTP tryConsume budget in verifyPhone but only compares 10 vs 5; it misses that the bucket is in-memory and that the OTP is never invalidated after failed guesses.
R8 reports the same timing leak: the unknown-login path skips bcrypt.
R6 notes that sendPasswordResetMail's paths fail differently and reveal account existence, but only through the dob-null NPE, not the PWD_RESET_REJECTED vs success response difference.
No finding covers per-IP-only throttling of resendVerificationEmail.
No finding covers activate.security=false having no profile guard.

unmatched_reported.note: Concrete trigger: concurrent same-key logins each sleep in the advisory-lock retry loop while holding a pooled connection, which can exhaust the Hikari pool.
Concrete trigger: a mixed-case email is stored raw as the login but looked up lower-cased, so that user can never log in.
Concrete trigger: legacy registerAccount stores the raw-case email as the login while login looks it up lower-cased, so a mixed-case registrant cannot authenticate.
Concrete trigger: save() without flush on app-assigned ids defers the unique-constraint violation to commit, outside the catch, so duplicate phone/email is not mapped to the registration error.
Concrete trigger: the grace branch picks the user's newest live token, rotating another device's token, and that device's next refresh revokes every session.
